honing_confound: Phoenix and Ancient Spear skill damage scales with Magic attack power (gear honing). Ancient Elemental summon effectiveness is also gear-indexed. Tier standing in current meta reflects T4 elemental burst ceiling.

delivery.evidence: Primary damage sources: Phoenix (targeted forward-charge summon with fire AoE), Ancient Spear (conjured spear for high single-target hit), Sylphid (wind-gust summon), Pauru (dog-type melee summon). Mix of targeted ranged AoE and on-location summon deployment.

footprint.evidence: Summons appear at caster and at target location depending on skill. Phoenix charges to target. Pauru/dog acts at target location. Not a single-point kit — multi-summon deployment creates distributed footprint.

geo_text: Summoner deploys Ancient Elemental spirits for direct damage. Master Summoner focuses on the 5 Ancient Elementals (Apnor, Mischief, Silf, Pauru, Asultan) as spending Ancient Energy for burst damage or utility summons. Skills mostly deploy summons at target location or in cones from caster. Safe range — caster stays back while summons act.

control.evidence: Some elemental summons apply knockback or slow (Sylphid = wind-based, likely slow). No primary CC identity — summons are damage-focused in Master Summoner.

defense.evidence: Mage archetype — glass profile. Some summon abilities may provide brief protection but not documented as identity defensive mechanics.

economy.builder_source: Normal skills generate Ancient Energy (Orbs). Ancient Elemental spells cost Orbs to cast. Master Summoner: Ancient Elemental skills enhanced — builder-spender loop where generating orbs via normals enables big elemental spends.
economy.plain_text: 5 ORB ECONOMY: Fill Orbs via normal skills → Spend Orbs to summon Ancient Elementals (each costs 1-3 orbs). Master Summoner enhances Ancient Elemental skill outputs specifically. Key skills: Phoenix (fire elemental, high damage, requires orbs), Ancient Spear (major damage spike). Strategy: generate orbs → spend on Phoenix/Spear for burst windows. Simple builder-spender with elemental theming.

element.evidence: Summoner's Ancient Elementals cover fire (Phoenix/Asultan), wind (Sylphid), earth (Pauru), and arcane types. Master Summoner uses multiple elements.

movement.evidence: Moderate mobility — summons act independently, giving the caster some freedom. Mage archetype — still rooted during major casts.

attr.evidence: Summons deploy to target location — caster can stay safe. Some summons act at caster (Pauru may be melee-adjacent) but overall kit allows safe positioning.

range.evidence: Estimated from ranged mage archetype. Not confirmed with exact distances.

tempo.evidence: Master Summoner is the burst identity: generate orbs → spend on powerful Ancient Elementals → rebuild. Phoenix and Ancient Spear are the burst tools. 'Quick bursts of damage' per search results.

amp.value: Ancient Elemental skills enhanced (Master Summoner identity); Phoenix and Ancient Spear as primary damage amplifiers
amp.evidence: Search results: 'Master Summoner enhances Ancient Elemental Skills' and 'quick bursts of damage; Phoenix and Ancient Spear are the main sources of damage.'

proxy.evidence: Ancient Elementals ARE proxy entities — summoned creatures that act independently. Pauru (dog) acts at target. Phoenix charges forward. Sylphid creates wind effect. SUMMONER IS THE CORPUS'S CLEAREST PROXY/SUMMON DELIVERY CLASS.

commitment.evidence: Summon-deploying skills in LA are typically instant-cast triggers (the summon then acts on its own). Not specifically documented from live sources.

mechanics_notes: 1) Master Summoner is the Summoner identity where Ancient Elementals ARE the primary output — the class functions like a traditional summoner (big powerful summons on cooldown via resource spending). Communication Overflow is the 'pet army' identity (persistent weaker summons). 2) Phoenix as a burst skill: fire elemental that charges to target dealing massive AoE — this is the signature Master Summoner moment and distinguishes it from other mage identities. 3) PROXY FLAG: Summoner is the most explicit proxy/summon class in the corpus. The 'delivery' field for Summoner doesn't fit cleanly into the standard schema — damage is delivered BY the proxy, not directly by the caster. Mechanics-gap note: our delivery taxonomy doesn't distinguish 'caster-directed projectile' from 'autonomous proxy entity that deals damage.' 4) Ancient Spear is a conjured physical spike — not a summoned creature but a created weapon projectile. Hybrid between 'at-target' delivery and proxy deployment.
stabilization_patch: Master Summoner identity was reworked for global launch (October 2022 addition). Communication Overflow was dominant initially; Master Summoner gained ground post-rework.
tier_standing_current: A-tier (Manillagames January 2026). HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: Ancient Elemental damage scales with Magic Power — higher honing = higher elemental damage.

honing_confound: Persistent pet damage scales with pet stats which may be boosted by gear-dependent passive buffs. Tier standing reflects meta where pet uptime and control is valued.

delivery.evidence: Communication Overflow emphasizes 'Pets' (smaller persistent summons): Pauru (earth/dog), Osh (water/bird), smaller elemental companions. These AI-controlled companions attack designated targets. Akir (the large summon) converts from damage to party BUFF in this identity.

footprint.evidence: Multiple persistent pets acting at different locations simultaneously — multi-point distributed footprint. Pets can be micromanaged (shift-command to target location).

geo_text: Communication Overflow Summoner maintains a persistent army of smaller elemental pets that continuously attack targets. The caster micromanages pets via shift-left-click targeting commands. Akir (normally a powerful single-summon damage skill) converts to a party buff in this identity. Safe-range play while pets do damage work.

control.evidence: Pet attack patterns don't emphasize CC. No primary control identity.

defense.evidence: Same mage glass profile. Pets provide no defensive layer to the caster.

economy.resource_verbatim: Ancient Energy (Orbs) — modified usage in Communication Overflow
economy.builder_source: Normal skills generate Orbs. Communication Overflow: pet summon costs reduced or modified — petarmony is maintained with fewer orb expenditures. Akir converts to buff spend.
economy.plain_text: PERSISTENT PET ECONOMY: Orbs are spent on deploying pets (smaller, persistent, continuous-attack creatures). Pets auto-attack designated targets and can be shift-commanded to move. Akir (the 'big summon' spend) converts from a damage source to a powerful party buff for Communication Overflow. Economy emphasis: maintain pet presence via moderate orb spending + periodic Akir buff activation.

element.evidence: Pets are elementally themed. Pauru = earth/dog, Osh = water/bird. Damage types match elemental theming.

movement.evidence: Same mage profile. Pets acting independently gives the caster more tactical freedom — can reposition while pets attack.

attr.evidence: Same safe-range positioning as Master Summoner.

tempo.evidence: Communication Overflow is the sustained identity: persistent pets deal continuous damage rather than burst windows. 'Bases most of its damage on her Pets which she can micro-manage' — sustained autonomous output.

amp.value: Akir converts to party buff (Communication Overflow exclusive); persistent pet damage as sustained output
amp.evidence: Search results: 'Communication Overflow Ark Passive line turns the Akir summon from a large damaging skill into a powerful buff for your normal summons.'

proxy.evidence: Communication Overflow is the stronger proxy/summon case of the two Summoner identities — persistent autonomous pets are pure proxy delivery. MORE PROXY than Master Summoner (which has burst summons vs CO's persistent ones).

commitment.evidence: Pet deployment and shift-commands are likely instant. Not specifically documented.

mechanics_notes: 1) Communication Overflow is the archetypal 'persistent summon' identity — pets act autonomously and continuously rather than as on-demand burst tools. This is the closest analogue in LA to a pet-class in ARPGs (D2 Necromancer, PoE Summoner, etc.). 2) Akir's conversion from damage to party buff is a meaningful identity-level transformation: the same skill changes function depending on the engraving. This is different from Master Summoner where Akir remains a damage source. 3) Micromanagement via shift-command is a unique control scheme in LA — no other class requires player-directed pet positioning commands. This is a mechanics-gap: our delivery vocabulary doesn't capture 'player-directed autonomous proxy' as distinct from 'player-activated proxy skill.' 4) SUPPORT-ADJACENT: The Akir buff conversion makes Communication Overflow slightly party-support-adjacent (not as dedicated as Bard/Paladin, but Akir buff benefits the party). Not a support class but has a support node in the identity.
stabilization_patch: Communication Overflow was the early dominant identity; Master Summoner became competitive post-rework. Both have seen tier movement with balance patches.
tier_standing_current: A-tier (2025-2026). HONING-CONFOUND NOTE: Pet damage output scaling is less straightforward to characterize than direct-cast damage — confound applies but less directly than in burst identities.
